algorithm: Compute the floor division of the inputs using the `//` operator in Python.
Ensure that the inputs are broadcasted to a common shape if necessary.
Return the result as a list if the inputs are not scalars, otherwise as a scalar.
constraints: All inputs must be integers or 1-D lists of integers.
No other broadcasting is required beyond the specified cases.
The result must fit within signed int64.
edge_cases: When the divisor is zero, an error is raised.
When the inputs are empty lists, the output is also an empty list.
When the inputs are of different shapes, they must be broadcasted to a common shape.
When the inputs are of different types (e.g., scalar and list), the result is a list.
inputs: x and y are integers or 1-D lists of integers. Support scalar/scalar, scalar/list, list/scalar and lists of the same length (including empty). Scalar/scalar returns int, all other inputs return a list. No other broadcasting is required. Values and results fit signed int64. Divisors are nonzero.
output: y: ndarray, which is a scalar if both x and y are scalars, otherwise a list of the same length as x.
purpose: Compute the floor division of two inputs, returning the largest integer less than or equal to the division result.
